defects.title: The save-before-serve phase writes nothing to the caller for its whole duration
defects.symptom: The FIRST request for a cold prefix is silent for the full prefix prefill: no HTTP status, no bytes, nothing — 100-145 s for a Claude-Code-sized head (22-27k tokens at ~200 t/s). Locally that is a long wait; through the Cloudflare tunnel it is a 524 after ~125 s, and the answer is thrown away while the save marches on. In the gateway journal the defect reads as an ABORTED at ~125 s followed by a SAVED a few seconds later — which looks like a client that gave up, not like anything the gateway did.
defects.measured: First seen live 31.08.2026 12:43: the operator's first streamed request from another machine (26,657 tokens, cold) died with a Cloudflare 524 at 124.9 s; the prewarm finished and saved at 144.3 s. Reproduced the same day with bench/suites/sse-ping.py against a cold 22k prefix, one run per point in the chain: gateway, pre-fix — first byte (the HTTP status line itself) at 114.5 s, 0 pings, largest gap 114.5 s. llama-server directly, same body — status after 0.2 s, a ':' ping at 30/60/90 s, message_start at 114.6 s, largest gap 30.1 s, so the server side is innocent and setup/README.md's keep-alive table holds on b10702-11 as well. Gateway with the fix — first ping at 30.0 s, pings at 30/60/90, message_start at 122.1 s, largest gap 32.0 s. CAUSE, read in the source: save_prefix_first (29.08. design, save BEFORE serve) runs the whole prewarm inside the request while the caller's response is not yet opened; llama-server never sees the request during it, so its own SSE pings cannot run, and the gateway's QUEUE_KEEPALIVE covers only the admission queue — the comment above it names the exact 125 s window this phase then reopened. INSTRUMENT FINDING, kept in the suite: a nonce in the system text does NOT make a prompt cold here — the rendered prompt carries the tool section first, so the divergence lands at ~90 % depth and llama reuses the rest (f_keep 0.892, 2,126 of 22,226 tokens recomputed). The suite plants a nonce TOOL at position 0 instead.
defects.mitigation: FIXED 31.08.2026, the same rules as the queue phase: save_prefix_first keeps a STREAMING caller alive — the response is opened on the first KEEPALIVE slice, ':' every slice, and a later upstream failure arrives as an SSE error event because the status is spent (sse_error, which forward() already handles for a prepared response). A non-streaming caller cannot be kept alive without committing its status code and stays untouched — scripts and curl tests without stream:true still run into the window, exactly as setup/README.md documents. Guarded by tests/test_gateway.py TestSavePhaseLifesign, seen red (TypeError x3) against the pre-fix code.

detect.how: python3 bench/suites/sse-ping.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8090 --body <a tools/synthetic.py file> against a COLD prefix: the SUMMARY's largest_gap must stay near KEEPALIVE (~30 s); before the fix it read 114.5 s. From the journal alone: an ABORTED at ~125 s followed within seconds by a SAVED for the same prefix is this defect seen from the log.

defects.status: FIXED AND LIVE since 31.08.2026 13:34 — the production gateway was restarted on the operator's go and now runs the fix. Verified END TO END through the Cloudflare edge with a case ABOVE the window, after the operator caught that the first verification run (114.4 s save phase) sat UNDER it and proved nothing about survival: a cold ~40k-token streamed request over the tunnel, save phase 253.8 s, got HTTP 200, 8 pings at a 30 s cadence and message_start at 262.3 s, largest gap 30.4 s, no 524 — more than double any window and past the incident's own 144 s. The journal shows the 'sign of life while the prefix is saved' line at exactly START+30 s on both runs, so the pings came from this code path and not from the queue phase. The fix is on branch test/sse-524 and NOT YET COMMITTED; until it is merged, a checkout of another branch plus a gateway restart would silently reintroduce the silence.

defects.title: Claude Code places static context behind the typed first message, so every fresh session recomputes it
defects.symptom: The first turn of a fresh Claude Code session (after /clear or a new start) recomputes ~4k tokens and takes ~25 s although everything it sends except the typed greeting is byte-identical to the previous session. The trace reads '84 % cache' with 'msgs N -> 2, kept 2' — system and tools held, the message area rewritten.
defects.measured: 31.08.2026, at trace level `text`, five fresh sessions from the same client. Anatomy of the request: system 8.8 KB + 52 tool schemas 99.4 KB = the 24,609-token head, always cached; then messages[0] = [system-reminder 306 chars, caveat 246, /clear metadata 177, THE TYPED MESSAGE]; then messages[1] = a 7,252-char static block (the Agent-tool type list), byte-identical between sessions. Four sessions opened with the identical word 'hi': reused=28490 computed=4, 0.9-1.4 s each — so the surrounding blocks are stable and the cache works. One session opened with 'hallo' instead: reused=24609 computed=3886, 25.3 s — the divergence sits exactly at the typed word, and everything behind it is recomputed, including the identical 7.3 KB. The prefix cache is doing exactly what a prefix cache does; the ordering puts variable text in front of static text. CONTRAST, same trace store 30.08.: the DeepSeek harness sends its large dynamic message first and carries no static trailer — 99.2 % cache over 39 turns, which is what the same stack does when the ordering is right. KNOWN UPSTREAM: claude-code #47098 reports this exact structure (cache_control only on the typed input, static reminders uncached before it, the same 'greet first' workaround) and was CLOSED AS NOT PLANNED in April 2026; #43657 and #27048 are the resume-side relatives.
defects.mitigation: NOT FIXABLE HERE, twice over. Reordering the messages in the gateway would change the prompt the model actually reads — the category of rewrite this stack deliberately keeps switched off (HOIST_SYSTEM=0 is the operator's standing decision), and it would break against every Claude Code release that moves the blocks again. Upstream knows and has closed it as not planned. WORKAROUND, measured: open every fresh session with the same constant word (e.g. exactly 'hi') and put the real question in the second turn — the first turn is then computed=4 and near-instant, and the second turn appends behind a warm prefix instead of diverging in front of 4k static tokens. Costs one greeting.

detect.how: In the journal: a fresh-session first turn with reused stuck at the head boundary (~24.6k here) and computed ~3.9k. In `tools/tracelog.py diff`: 'msgs N -> 2, kept 2' right after a /clear. At trace level `text` the two bodies differ only in the typed block of messages[0].

defects.status: OPEN as a property of the client, documented 31.08.2026. Nothing to fix in this stack; the workaround stands in `mitigation` and costs one greeting per session. Re-check the message order after Claude Code updates — #43657 shows the blocks have moved before.

defects.title: A prompt that diverges near its end is rolled back to the last checkpoint, not to the divergence
defects.symptom: Two prompts share a long head and differ only near the end — same system, same tools, a different final user text. The reuse does not reach the divergence: it stops at the last context checkpoint of the PREVIOUS prompt, and everything from there is recomputed. Here that turned a ~170-token difference into a 2,050-token recompute, ~10 s instead of ~1 s, once per changed prompt.
defects.measured:
31.08.2026, DeepSeek-harness traffic against qwen38, trace level text, positions confirmed with /apply-template + /tokenize (tools included in the template call — the slot-tail.py lesson). The prompt: head (system message + 52 tools) = 8,081 tokens, the harness start prompt = 16 tokens at position 8,081, a 154-token runtime-context message BEHIND it, total 8,251. Identical rerun: reused=8245..8247, computed=4 — the end-minus-4 checkpoint, f_keep 1.0. Changed start prompt: reused=6201, computed=2050. The arithmetic is exact: 6,201 = 8,249 (previous prompt) - 2,048 (n_ubatch), and 2,050 = 2,048 + 2 — the slot fell back to the previous prompt's last usable checkpoint, 1,880 tokens BEFORE the true divergence at 8,081. checkpoints exist only at {end-4, end-(4+n_ubatch)} of what was processed (server-context.cpp checkpoint_offsets), and a hybrid slot cannot be trimmed to an arbitrary position — llama_memory_hybrid::seq_pos_min sits at the sequence end, the same amplifier the-previous-answer-is-sometimes-not-reused documents. So 1,880 of the 2,050 recomputed tokens are checkpoint rounding, not content. The client's share is small here: the harness carries only the 154-token runtime-context behind the variable input — the same ordering flaw as static-context-sits-behind-the-first-typed-message, at 1/25 the size.

REPRODUCED AND EXPLAINED the same afternoon on a side server (bench/reports/2026-08-31_1500_checkpoint-grid): a changed prompt sent STRAIGHT after its predecessor reuses to the EXACT divergence (reused=8074, computed=177) even on the default grid — the rounding needs the production-shaped history of an identical repeat plus the harness's judge calls in between (sequence a,j,a,j,b). Every reprocessing lays fresh end checkpoints and the min-step eviction (default 8192) then prunes the user-message-boundary checkpoint as too close; the best rollback point left is one ubatch before the previous end, which is exactly where reused lands (6201 = 8249 - 2048, reproduced deterministically, twice in one run). WITH --checkpoint-min-step 512, same sequence: reused=8074, computed=177/181 — the boundary checkpoint survives and the rounding is gone, 11.6x less prefill per task switch.
defects.mitigation: THE LEVER IS MEASURED and it is `--checkpoint-min-step 512` (default 8192): same production-shaped sequence, computed per changed start prompt falls from 2,050 to 177 tokens and reuse reaches the exact divergence. APPLIED 31.08.2026 ~15:30 — the flag is in setup/env/qwen38.env with the argument in its comment, and `status` carries the live verification (an earlier version of this field said 'NOT APPLIED yet'; it was written before the operator's go and outlived it). The price is more surviving checkpoints at 149.8 MiB each (capacity 32 per slot, and the RAM prompt cache stores them with every prompt); what that does to the -cram budget under real traffic is UNMEASURED and is the watch named in `status`. Secondary and mostly moot next to it: the harness could move its runtime-context message in front of the variable input (saves only the ~170 content tokens); `--ctx-checkpoints` (capacity, default 32) was never the limit.

detect.how: In the journal: a warm request whose reused equals the PREVIOUS prompt's length minus n_ubatch (here 2,048) while computed is n_ubatch plus a small remainder — on a prompt whose true divergence sits far behind the reuse point. /apply-template + /tokenize on the shared head gives the true divergence position; the gap between it and `reused` is the rounding.

defects.status: FIXED IN PRODUCTION 31.08.2026 ~15:30, on the operator's go: --checkpoint-min-step 512 is in setup/env/qwen38.env (with the argument in its comment) and VERIFIED LIVE after the restart — the production-shaped sequence shows reused=8074 computed=177 on the changed task prompt, where the default gave 6201/2050 the same afternoon. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is the memory side: checkpoints cost 149.8 MiB each, the finer grid keeps more of them, and the -cram fill rate under a real working day is unmeasured. Baseline for that watch: RssAnon 0.45 GiB at the 15:2x restart, cache empty. If the cache starts evicting noticeably, raise the step to 1024/2048 before raising -cram. Upstream family unchanged.
